answer: Identity Pulse Attestation. Each agent periodically emits a signed liveness pulse derived from a hardware-seeded cipher keyed to a unique physical root; duplicate roots produce correlated pulse timing that registries can cross-match. Agents must also submit a basalt-derived entropy sample from a local sensor, which varies per device and is costly to fabricate at scale. Duplicating an identity requires acquiring distinct hardware, sensors, and clock sources, raising marginal cost per sybil to near the cost of a genuine agent.
